title: Three Nights and One Short Sign
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：highway　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 highway 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the driver ① crossed the highway that no engineer in the depot would have described, and he said the crossing was the whole of the night. The ② highway, meaning the road itself and not the sign, ran three nights and stayed undescribed in the book; a highway, he said, is the only thing in a depot that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ highway in that depot had the same short sign beside it, and the ④ highway at the far bridge, meaning the route they kept for the children to travel and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A highway, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the driver said the describing is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the highway was the whole of the matter, meaning the journey and not the road. The ⑥ highway, meaning the journey and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; highway, he said, is either something you cross or the only word that means both a road and a journey. He said the journey is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ highway had become a line in a map, and the map had become an argument about the short sign. The ⑧ highway of the whole thing, the driver wrote in June, was one depot and three nights of describing; highway, he said, is either the route at the far bridge or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ highway I remember is the road described in the map, which closed in 1972 and is still described as the quietest in the depot. A ⑩ highway, my mother said in 1974, is the only road that improves by being described; every highway, she said, is a journey that has agreed to look like a road. She said the journey was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 公路；干道（指车站里每一条旁边的那一条）
B. n. 公路；干道（指那条干道本身，与路牌相对）
C. 固定搭配：cross the highway 穿过这条公路
D. n. 公路；干道（指留给孩子们学着走的那一条）
E. n. 路途之事（抽象总称，指一处车站的公路之事）
F. n. 公路；干道（指地图里写到、被记下的的那一条）
G. n. 旅途、行程（指一件事里人人都走却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 行程（抽象总称，指人人都走却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: crossed the highway that no engineer in the depot would have described
The highway, meaning the road itself and not the sign
the highway at the far bridge
the highway was the whole of the matter
the highway had become a line in a map
The highway of the whole thing
A highway, my mother said in 1974

answers.why: cross the highway 意为“穿过这条公路”，1965 年那位司机把车站里没有一位工程师肯描述的一条公路做了一遍。
highway 意为“公路；干道”，指那条干道本身而不是路牌，它经过了三个夜而在簿子上没有被描述。
highway 意为“公路；干道”，指车站里每一条旁边的那一条，每一条旁边都有同一块小小的路牌。
highway 意为“公路；干道”，指最远那座桥头留给孩子们学着走的那一条，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
highway 意为“旅途、行程”，指一件事里人人都走却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这段旅途就是那件事的全部。
highway 意为“行程”，指人人都走却无人提起的那样东西而不是那条干道，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
highway 意为“公路；干道”，指地图里写到、被记下的的那一条，到 1970 年这一条成了地图里的一行。
highway 意为“路途之事”，司机六月写道，整件事的公路之事是一处车站和三个夜的描述。
highway 意为“公路；干道”，我记得的是地图里描述过的那一条，1972 年改线了，至今仍被说成车站里最安静的一条。
highway 为抽象总称，母亲 1974 年说，公路是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的干道。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1965 年那位司机穿过了车站里没有一位工程师肯描述的一条公路，他说这一遍才是那个夜的全部。（cross the highway）
那条公路，指的是那条干道本身而不是路牌，经过了三个夜而在簿子上没有被描述。（highway）
那处车站里每一条公路旁边都有同一块小小的路牌。（highway）
最远那座桥头那条公路，指的是他们留给孩子们学着走的那一条，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（highway）
叔叔说这段旅途就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那条干道。（highway）
1974 年母亲说，公路是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的干道。（highway）
answers: In 1965 the driver crossed the highway that no engineer in the depot would have described, and he said the crossing was the whole of the night.
The highway, meaning the road itself and not the sign, ran three nights and stayed undescribed in the book.
Every highway in that depot had the same short sign beside it.
The highway at the far bridge, meaning the route they kept for the children to travel and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the highway was the whole of the matter, meaning the journey and not the road.
A highway, my mother said in 1974, is the only road that improves by being described.
